meta.title: Engineering AI Profile & Skill Builder
meta.description: Bilingual (EN/FA) open-source tool for industrial and EPC engineering teams to build verified, reusable AI profiles and domain skill instructions.

hero.title: Build Verified AI Profiles for Professional Engineering Teams
hero.subtitle: Create structured, discipline-grounded instructions for ChatGPT, Claude, Microsoft Copilot, or local LLMs. Tailored for heavy industry, metal plants, utilities, and EPC/EPCM projects with zero hallucinated standards.

disclaimer.title: Professional Engineering Verification Notice
disclaimer.text: This application generates deterministic text prompts and reusable instructions for AI assistants. It does NOT perform engineering calculations, finite element analysis, or code certification. All outputs produced by third-party AI systems must be independently checked, verified, and stamped by qualified professional engineers before being used in tender, design, procurement, or construction activities.

privacyNotice.title: Client-Side Privacy Guarantee
privacyNotice.text: All profile generation, saving, and export happens 100% locally in your web browser. No project data, job descriptions, or custom instructions are ever sent to an external server or analytics service. Do NOT paste proprietary, classified, or confidential plant telemetry into unauthorized public AI chatbots.

experienceLevels.senior: Senior Specialist / Lead Discipline Engineer (8-15 years)
experienceLevels.principal: Principal Engineer / Chief Technical Specialist (15+ years)

tech_writing.name: Technical Writing & Design Criteria
tech_writing.desc: Clear, objective, unambiguous engineering prose with defined terminology and passive/active consistency.
tech_writing.prompt: Enforce rigorous technical writing standards: use objective, unambiguous language; define all acronyms upon first usage; formulate clear requirements with 'shall' for mandatory criteria, 'should' for recommendations, and 'may' for optional items; avoid vague qualitative assertions like 'optimal' or 'adequate' without verifiable numerical thresholds.

ms_word.name: Microsoft Word Document Structuring
ms_word.desc: Guidance for structured engineering specs, formal tables, numbered clauses, and cross-references.
ms_word.prompt: When structuring documentation intended for Microsoft Word: organize into hierarchical numbered sections (1.0, 1.1, 1.1.1); recommend clean table layouts with standard header formatting; suggest caption styles for figures and tables; structure appendices logically; ensure content is ready for copy-pasting into corporate document templates without formatting artifacts.

ms_excel.name: Microsoft Excel Calculations & Formulations
ms_excel.desc: Engineering spreadsheets, dynamic formulas, formula documentation, and sanity check tables.
ms_excel.prompt: When assisting with Microsoft Excel engineering tools: provide clean, robust cell formulas (e.g., INDEX/MATCH, XLOOKUP, LET, IFS); structure inputs, intermediate calculations, and final output summary blocks clearly; include cell formatting and unit conventions; suggest built-in error checks (data validation, boundary warnings); when requested, provide clean VBA or macros with thorough comments.

ms_powerpoint.name: Executive & Technical Presentations
ms_powerpoint.desc: Structured slide narratives, technical graphics recommendations, and bullet points for leadership.
ms_powerpoint.prompt: When outlining technical presentation decks: structure slides around one key takeaway per slide; formulate punchy, information-dense headlines rather than generic category titles; balance technical rigor with visual clarity; organize trade-offs into comparative 3-column matrices; format bullet points as actionable conclusions rather than raw data dumps.

meetings_actions.name: Meeting Minutes & Action Item Tracking
meetings_actions.desc: Professional Minutes of Meeting (MoM), decisions log, action item matrices, and punch lists.
meetings_actions.prompt: When drafting Minutes of Meeting (MoM) or action item trackers: strictly document: (1) Meeting Objective & Date, (2) Key Discussions & Agreed Decisions, (3) Numbered Action Item Table containing Action ID, Task Description, Responsible Person/Discipline, and Hard Due Date; maintain neutral, objective factual wording; avoid emotional tone.

formal_correspondence.name: Formal Engineering Correspondence & Transmittals
formal_correspondence.desc: Formal contractual letters, client transmittals, requests for information (RFI), and variation notices.
formal_correspondence.prompt: When drafting formal engineering correspondence, RFIs, or document transmittal cover letters: use professional contractual engineering language; state the precise project name, contract/work package reference, and specific document numbers; clearly separate contractual notices from technical clarifications; specify the required response timeframe.

doc_review_crs.name: Document Review & Comment Resolution Sheets (CRS)
doc_review_crs.desc: Structured technical comments, code references, severity classifications (Major/Minor/Typo), and responses.
doc_review_crs.prompt: When conducting engineering document reviews or populating Comment Resolution Sheets (CRS): structure comments with Document Number, Page/Paragraph/Clause Reference, Review Comment with Engineering Justification, Proposed Corrective Action, and Severity (Major / Minor / Editorial); formulate comments constructively with direct citations to project specifications or codes.

data_analysis.name: Technical Data Analysis & Statistical Trends
data_analysis.desc: Analyzing industrial test records, process measurements, lab assays, and performance curves.
data_analysis.prompt: When analyzing engineering data or test trends: compute and state descriptive statistical metrics (mean, standard deviation, min, max, percentile); identify outliers and potential measurement anomalies; compare data against baseline design thresholds; present findings in structured Markdown comparison tables with explicit engineering units.

technical_reporting.name: Technical Inspection & Feasibility Reports
technical_reporting.desc: Site inspection reports, failure analyses, root-cause investigations, and technology assessments.
technical_reporting.prompt: When drafting technical investigation or inspection reports: maintain the standard engineering structure: Executive Summary, Background & Scope, Observations & Methodology, Technical Findings, Root Cause Analysis, and Prioritized Recommendations; clearly separate physical field observations from theoretical analytical deductions.

project_coordination.name: Interdisciplinary EPC Coordination
project_coordination.desc: Interface management, battery limits, civil-mechanical-electrical battery limits, and clash management.
project_coordination.prompt: When coordinating interdisciplinary EPC issues: proactively identify and document physical, electrical, and process interfaces; specify physical battery limits (B/L) and tie-in points with coordinates/elevations; detail loads transferred between disciplines (e.g., dynamic equipment loads on civil foundations); highlight lead times for long-lead interface items.

civil_structural.name: Civil & Structural Engineering
civil_structural.desc: Concrete foundations, structural steel, wind/seismic load combinations, and connection design.
civil_structural.prompt: For Civil and Structural Engineering tasks: strictly adhere to international codes (e.g., AISC 360, ACI 318, Eurocodes, ASCE 7); explicitly state all load combinations (Dead, Live, Wind, Seismic, Equipment Operating/Empty/Hydrotest, Thermal); distinguish between serviceability limit states (deflections, vibrations) and ultimate strength limit states; specify member profiles, steel grades, rebar cover, and concrete characteristic strengths; provide clear calculation steps with governing formulas.

mechanical_equip.name: Mechanical Equipment (Static & Rotating)
mechanical_equip.desc: Pumps, compressors, pressure vessels, tanks, heat exchangers, material handling, and datasheets.
mechanical_equip.prompt: For Mechanical Equipment tasks: reference applicable standards (e.g., ASME Section VIII, API 650, API 610, ISO 13709); for rotating equipment, highlight operating points, NPSHa vs NPSHr margins, driver sizing factors, vibration limits, and lubrication requirements; for static equipment, state design pressure/temperature, corrosion allowance, radiography factors, and nozzle schedules; require full datasheets with operating vs design conditions.

electrical_power.name: Electrical Systems (Power, MV/LV & Substation)
electrical_power.desc: Single-line diagrams, load flow, short circuit, cable sizing, motor control, and earthing.
electrical_power.prompt: For Electrical Power tasks: reference standards such as IEC 60364, IEC 60909, IEEE 141/399; clearly structure electrical load lists with continuous, intermittent, and standby loads including diversity and power factors; in short-circuit and protection evaluations, state peak and breaking capacities; specify voltage levels, transformer impedance, cable derating factors (ambient temp, grouping, burial depth), and earthing/lightning protection requirements.

process_metallurgy.name: Process Engineering & Metallurgy
process_metallurgy.desc: Mass & heat balances, PFDs, P&IDs, hydraulics, relief valve sizing, and chemical metallurgy.
process_metallurgy.prompt: For Process Engineering and Metallurgy tasks: verify mass, molar, and energy balance conservation; explicitly detail stream parameters (temperature, pressure, phase fraction, density, viscosity, mass flow rate); for P&ID reviews, specify piping classes, valve types, slope requirements, instrumentation loops, interlocks, and fail-safe valve positions; evaluate overpressure scenarios and relief sizing in accordance with API 520/521.

piping_stress.name: Piping Engineering & Stress Analysis
piping_stress.desc: Piping specifications, wall thickness, flexibility/stress analysis, tie-in schedules, and supports.
piping_stress.prompt: For Piping Engineering tasks: comply with ASME B31.3 / B31.1; verify pipe wall thickness calculations under internal design pressure, corrosion allowance, and mill tolerance; consider thermal expansion, nozzle load allowable limits on connected equipment, and seismic/slug load cases in flexibility reviews; formulate comprehensive tie-in lists with coordinate locations, isolation philosophy, hot-tap feasibility, and shutdown durations.

instrumentation_control.name: Instrumentation & Control (I&C / DCS / PLC)
instrumentation_control.desc: Instrument index, I/O lists, control narratives, loop diagrams, SIL/SIS, and field transmitters.
instrumentation_control.prompt: For Instrumentation & Control tasks: specify instrument technology based on process medium, hazardous area classification (ATEX/IECEx/NEC), and process conditions; organize I/O lists with tag, service description, signal type (AI, AO, DI, DO, Fieldbus), range, alarm setpoints, and fail-safe state; formulate functional control narratives and cause-and-effect matrices (C&E); address Safety Instrumented Systems (SIS) according to IEC 61508 / 61511.

hvac_ventilation.name: HVAC & Industrial Ventilation
hvac_ventilation.desc: Control room pressurization, battery room exhaust, cooling/heating loads, and air change rates.
hvac_ventilation.prompt: For HVAC & Industrial Ventilation tasks: compute sensible and latent thermal loads; specify room design conditions (temperature, relative humidity, positive/negative differential pressure); enforce air change rates per hour (ACH) based on hazard classification (e.g., NFPA for battery rooms or electrical substation pressurization); detail filtration stages (pre-filters, HEPA, chemical carbon filters for toxic industrial environments); specify equipment redundancy (N+1).

construction_erection.name: Construction & Field Erection Engineering
construction_erection.desc: Constructability reviews, heavy lift rigging studies, erection sequences, and site inspection test plans.
construction_erection.prompt: For Construction & Erection tasks: focus on practical site execution feasibility, sequencing, and access clearances; review heavy lift plans noting crane capacities, boom angles, ground bearing pressure, and rigging safety factors; detail Inspection and Test Plans (ITP) with Hold, Witness, and Review points; address site welding procedures (WPS/PQR), bolt torquing protocols, and pre-alignment tolerances.

procurement_tbe.name: Procurement & Technical Bid Evaluation (TBE)
procurement_tbe.desc: Material requisitions, vendor technical evaluations, deviation lists, and submittal review cycles.
procurement_tbe.prompt: For Technical Procurement tasks: structure Technical Bid Evaluations (TBE) into clear compliance matrices: Scope of Supply, Technical Compliance with Specification, Deviations & Exceptions, Sub-vendor List, Spare Parts & Special Tools, and Delivery Schedule; mark vendor deviations explicitly as Acceptable, Acceptable with Clarification, or Unacceptable; maintain strict objective fairness without bias.

planning_project_controls.name: Planning, Scheduling & Project Controls
planning_project_controls.desc: Work Breakdown Structure (WBS), Primavera P6 schedule logic, Critical Path Method (CPM), and S-curves.
planning_project_controls.prompt: For Planning & Project Controls tasks: develop logically linked Work Breakdown Structures (WBS) down to work package level; audit schedule networks for proper logic links (predecessors, successors) avoiding arbitrary lead/lag constraints; calculate Total Float and identify the Critical Path; evaluate progress using Earned Value Analysis (PV, EV, AC, CPI, SPI); project milestone completion dates and suggest schedule recovery measures.

detailLevel.brief: Executive / Concise (Bullet points, key conclusions, direct numbers)
detailLevel.balanced: Balanced / Standard (Clear explanations with structured details)
detailLevel.rigorous: Deep Engineering Rigor (Full calculation steps, derivations, comprehensive clauses)

askClarifications.label: Ask Clarifying Questions
askClarifications.desc: If design inputs, battery limits, or process conditions are missing or ambiguous, ask before making critical assumptions.

stateAssumptions.label: Explicitly State Assumptions
stateAssumptions.desc: State all baseline parameters, design temperatures, ambient conditions, and material grades assumed.

showFormulas.label: Show Formulas & Calculation Steps
showFormulas.desc: Include governing engineering equations, substituted numerical values, intermediate steps, and dimensional unit checks.

strictStandards.label: Reference Recognized Industry Codes & Standards
strictStandards.desc: Cite official standards (ISO, ASME, ASTM, IEEE, API, DIN, EN) accurately. Never invent fictitious clause numbers, revision years, or ASTM grades.

engineeringChecklists.label: Provide Verification & QA/QC Checklists
engineeringChecklists.desc: Include actionable engineering checklists for design reviews, model audits, or document handover.

safetyRisks.label: Highlight Process Safety & Environmental Risks
safetyRisks.desc: Flag hazardous areas, toxic releases, overpressure scenarios, thermal expansion stresses, and constructability hazards.

disciplineInterfaces.label: Highlight Interdisciplinary Interfaces
disciplineInterfaces.desc: Explicitly call out impacts on other disciplines (e.g., dynamic equipment weights on civil foundations, electrical loads for I&C).

tabularFormat.label: Use Structured Tables for Complex Data
tabularFormat.desc: Present equipment schedules, comparison studies, bill of quantities, and technical trade-offs in clean Markdown tables.

factsVsAssumptions.label: Distinguish Verified Project Data from Assumptions
factsVsAssumptions.desc: Clearly label confirmed client specifications as [VERIFIED FACT] and inferred values as [ASSUMPTION - SUBJECT TO VERIFICATION].

howItWorks.title: How to Use This Profile Builder in Your Engineering Workflow

step1.title: 1. Configure Your Professional Persona
step1.desc: Specify your discipline, experience level, plant type, and key engineering software tools. This ensures the AI understands your technical vocabulary and expected engineering deliverable standards.

step2.title: 2. Select Professional & Discipline Skill Modules
step2.desc: Choose relevant communication, calculation, drafting, and discipline-specific technical rules. Each module injects proven, real-world EPC guidelines into your instructions.

step3.title: 3. Calibrate Rigor & Anti-Hallucination Guardrails
step3.desc: Turn on strict citation rules, calculation displays, and assumption separation. This prevents AI chatbots from fabricating phantom standard clauses or making unstated engineering leaps.

step4.title: 4. Paste into Your AI Assistant
step4.desc: Copy the generated prompt into ChatGPT 'Custom Instructions', Claude 'Project System Prompt', Microsoft Copilot, or your internal enterprise LLM. Save or export your JSON profile for future project reuse.

ALL DESIGNS, MATERIAL SELECTIONS, SIZING CALCULATIONS, AND SPECIFICATIONS MUST BE INDEPENDENTLY CALCULATED, AUDITED, AND STAMPED BY A QUALIFIED, LICENSED PROFESSIONAL ENGINEER IN ACCORDANCE WITH APPLICABLE JURISDICTIONAL LAWS AND PROJECT SPECIFICATIONS BEFORE TENDER, PROCUREMENT, OR CONSTRUCTION.
